Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Travel & transport

direct adjective

straight, without turning or stopping: a direct route

also directly, straight, straight there, a direct flight, the most direct way, in a straight line, go straight home

classical

Ter. Eun. 87: cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?
Traupman 213: volāre rēctā in Austriam, to fly directly to Austria
Traupman 203, 304: directly, rēctā, per dīrēctum
Traupman 204: in a straight line, per dīrēctum

rēctus, rēcta, rēctum

adjective; the adverb rēctā (viā), straight, directly, declension

straight, direct

To go straight there is rēctā īre, with viā understood (see straight on).

Other words

  • dīrēctus, dīrēcta, dīrēctum — straight, direct, in a straight line

    adjective (participle of dīrigō), declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.144: sī simplex et dīrēctum patēret; Caes. BC 3.79.2: iter (Lewis & Short); Traupman 386

    In a straight line is in dīrēctō or per dīrēctum (Varr. LL 7.15; Plin. NH 5.80; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Quis hīc loquitur? ehem, tūne hīc erās, mī Phaedria? Quid hīc stābās? cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?

    Who’s that talking? Oh, it’s you, my dear Phaedria! Why were you standing out here? Why didn’t you come straight in?Ter. Eun. 86–87

  • flexuōsum iter habet, nē quid intrāre possit, sī simplex et dīrēctum patēret

    it has a winding passage, so that nothing can get in, as it could if the way lay open, simple and directCic. N.D. 2.144

  • Ī (īte) rēctā domum!

    Go straight home!Traupman 386

See also straight on, direct, flight.
